# Review

## Summary

The main claim is that harness code can take over much of an autonomous selection-based learning loop, which leaves three semantic competences on the frozen base LLM. Almost all of the side material supports that claim where it sits.

- **The three harness bullets and the remark about code-writing LLMs** say what gets offloaded. Without them, the "much of the loop" half of the claim has no content.
- **The criterion-revision paragraph** sets a boundary. It explains why store maintenance and double-loop revision do not add a fourth competence. That protects the count in the title.
- **The independence paragraph** explains why the competences are listed as three rather than one general semantic capacity. Only its last sentence, about the bootstrap procedure, goes beyond what the argument needs. That sentence is recorded as an INFO finding.
- **The harness-evolution ceiling illustration** is stated narrowly and supports the premise that a base-model floor exists even when the store can be updated.
- **The Scope and Open Questions sections** limit the hypothesis and frame what to measure next. They do not open new claims.

No branch competes strongly enough with the main claim to need removal.

# Review

## Core claim

Stated in one sentence from the note's own commitments: in an autonomous selection-based learning loop with frozen weights, harness code can take over enforcement, evidence capture and replay, and store bookkeeping, and as a working hypothesis this leaves three semantic competences on the base LLM: interpreting unformalized text into action, diagnosing novel failures and synthesizing candidates, and judging unformalized trade-offs while recognizing missing evidence.

## Prominence

The title and description state this two-part claim directly. The body opens with it and uses the order the claim needs. First comes the offload list, then the relocation-not-elimination pivot, then the three numbered competences in bold. Later sections stay subordinate. Store maintenance and criterion revision reduce to competences 2 and 3. The independence paragraph explains why the split is useful. The ingest gives a bounded illustration of a base-model floor. The Scope section restates the hypothesis status. None of this competes with the main claim.

The one shape issue is minor. The three competences arrive only after a bulleted list and a transition paragraph. In that paragraph, the sentence about the LLM building its own harness tools adds a side point instead of moving the argument forward. The claim is still easy to find and remember, so this is INFO, not WARN.

# Review

The note is compact for a claim with three named competences, a reduction of store maintenance and an empirical illustration. Most details are proportionate to their role.

The three-item harness list is the only place where enumeration runs slightly past its job. It is the premise for "much of the loop's machinery", so concreteness earns some space. Yet the same items recur in two later sentences, and each bullet carries three or four examples where two would establish the category. This is borderline, so it is reported as INFO rather than WARN.

Non-obvious passes:

- Each numbered competence is one sentence plus one link. It states what the model must do and where the concept is developed. Compressing it further would leave the competence named but not distinguishable from the others.
- The independence paragraph ("A model may follow clear prose procedures while still misdiagnosing noisy traces...") gives one contrast example. That contrast is what makes the separation actionable for the bootstrap, so it earns its two sentences.
- The Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling paragraph is a short source setup with its bound stated ("Even within one benchmark and loop"). It supplies the note's only empirical support and is already minimal.
- The Scope bullets are one-line boundary conditions that a working hypothesis needs.

Most of the note earns its space. Each of the three competences states a distinct requirement and links to the note that develops it. The store-maintenance paragraph does necessary work: it explains why there is no fourth competence for criterion revision or store upkeep. The second Scope bullet (necessary, not sufficient) adds a boundary that appears nowhere else. The open questions are new.

Two passages fail the deletion test in their current form. The first Scope bullet repeats the "working hypothesis" label a third time and adds a defensive contrast clause; only its revision rule is new. ---
description: "Working hypothesis: harness code can supply much of an autonomous selection-based learning loop, leaving three conjectured semantic competences on the frozen base LLM"
type: types/note.md

# Harness code may offload much of a selection loop, leaving three base LLM competences

**Working hypothesis.** Holding model weights fixed while updating a store of procedures, hypotheses, and code does not remove dependence on the base model's weights. Yet an autonomous [selection-based learning](./definitions/selection-based-learning.md) loop does not need the frozen LLM to perform every loop function on its own. Following [scheduler–LLM separation](./scheduler-llm-separation-exploits-an-error-correction-asymmetry.md), harness code can take over much of the loop's machinery:

- **Enforcement and context assembly:** running codified validators and schemas, routing and loading the relevant artifacts, and enforcing token budgets.
- **Evidence capture and replay:** recording which artifacts loaded during a run, annotating telemetry coverage gaps, replaying past cases, and running targeted ablations or bisects.
- **Store bookkeeping:** tracking unused or stale entries, flagging rising failure rates, scheduling periodic reviews, and executing rollbacks.

Because an LLM that writes code can also build new harness tools for those jobs, the frozen model does not need to keep track of budgets, traces, or regression suites in its head. Harness code can relocate mechanical and structural work, yet [semantic work can be relocated without being eliminated](./semantic-work-can-be-relocated-but-not-eliminated.md). In open-ended work where new failure modes, commitments, and remedies keep arriving, our working hypothesis is that three irreducible semantic competences remain on the frozen base LLM:

1. **Interpreting unformalized text into action.** The model must read natural-language procedures, hypotheses, and constraints that have not yet been codified into code and let them govern its behavior under realistic context loads ([operative change](./definitions/operative-change.md)).
2. **Diagnosing novel failures and synthesizing candidates across text and code.** It must turn an unanticipated failure and its trace into a causal diagnosis and propose novel remedies—new procedures, testable hypotheses, checks, or executable harness code ([diagnostic richness](./diagnostic-richness-constrains-outer-loop-learning-quality.md)).
3. **Judging unformalized trade-offs and recognizing missing evidence.** It must weigh competing consequences against stated commitments where no fixed check settles the choice, keep genuinely contested or under-evidenced comparisons open, and recognize when an existing check is misleading ([on-balance judgment with an LLM](./on-balance-judgment-with-an-llm.md)).

Under this split, store-level maintenance and [criterion revision](./definitions/single-loop-and-double-loop-learning.md) do not require a separate model competence. Detecting bloat, stale entries, or rising regressions belongs to harness code; spotting semantic conflicts between prose rules, refactoring them into a cleaner abstraction, or proposing a revised check reduces to competences 2 and 3 applied to the store and its criteria.

These three competences can fail independently and sit at different capability thresholds. A model may follow clear prose procedures while still misdiagnosing noisy traces or overclaiming certainty on incomplete records. Separating them lets a human-assisted bootstrap identify which competence currently binds: people temporarily supply the missing semantic step while transfer tests check each kind of decision on its own.

A bounded empirical illustration of a base-model floor appears in [Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling](../sources/harness-evolution-ceiling-weight-training.ingest.md), where the three weakest tested models produced no held-out gains under the same harness-evolution loop that improved stronger models. Even within one benchmark and loop, an inadequate base model can block outer-loop learning before the store itself saturates.

## Scope

- This split is a **working hypothesis**, not an established impossibility result. Any sub-task shown to be reliably offloadable to harness code moves out of the LLM column, and concrete bottlenecks discovered in practice can add to it.
- Clearing these competences is proposed as necessary for operating the loop autonomously, not sufficient for sustained continual learning.

## Open Questions

- Which of the three competences binds first on current frontier models in real software and knowledge-base maintenance?
- How far can better harness interfaces—such as structured replay harnesses, dependency graphs, and explicit coverage annotations—lower the base-model floor required for competences 2 and 3?

---

Relevant Notes:

- [Selection-based learning](./definitions/selection-based-learning.md) — defined-in: the loop whose autonomous operation sets these prerequisites
- [Scheduler–LLM separation exploits an error-correction asymmetry](./scheduler-llm-separation-exploits-an-error-correction-asymmetry.md) — grounds: why bookkeeping, replay, and enforceable checks belong in harness code while semantic interpretation stays on the model
- [Semantic work can be relocated, not eliminated](./semantic-work-can-be-relocated-but-not-eliminated.md) — grounds: why harness offloading narrows the base-LLM floor without eliminating it
- [On-balance judgment with an LLM](./on-balance-judgment-with-an-llm.md) — extends: develops competence 3 and how to test an LLM selector
- [Single-loop and double-loop learning](./definitions/single-loop-and-double-loop-learning.md) — defined-in: criterion revision, treated here as competences 2 and 3 applied to working checks
- [Operative change](./definitions/operative-change.md) — defined-in: why loading a prose procedure without behavioral dependence fails competence 1
- [Diagnostic richness constrains outer-loop learning quality](./diagnostic-richness-constrains-outer-loop-learning-quality.md) — extends: how the harness's evidence interface interacts with competence 2
- [Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling](../sources/harness-evolution-ceiling-weight-training.ingest.md) — evidenced-by: weak-model lines produced no held-out harness gains under a loop that lifted stronger models (bounded to one benchmark and loop)

---
description: "Synthesize a compression review into at most three high-level simplifications that materially improve the artifact but still require authorial judgment"
type: types/instruction.md

# Synthesize high-impact simplification opportunities

Read the complete artifact and the individual compression findings. Report only opportunities likely to materially improve a reader's understanding of the central claim, conceptual structure, or argumentative flow. Do not edit the artifact.

An opportunity qualifies when its benefit would be large but its implementation requires broader judgment. Typical cases include surfacing a buried thesis, making the role of a load-bearing paragraph explicit, combining several local findings into one deletion or fold, or reorganizing an explanation whose current sequence hides the argument. Exclude local wording improvements, cosmetic changes, minor compression, and alternatives that are merely different.

The synthesis may combine several gate findings or identify a global reorganization visible only after reading the artifact as a whole. Ground every opportunity in the artifact or the gate findings; do not invent a stronger thesis for the artifact to serve.

Distinguish a buried contribution from an undetermined one. A contribution supported by the artifact can be surfaced or given a clearer role. If the artifact does not select among materially different theses, audiences, or purposes, report the missing choice under `Preserve or decide`; do not choose one merely to make the prose cohere. This isolated synthesis receives no retained-intent input, so do not import the choice from the topic, a bare writing prompt, or ambient conversation. The calling workflow may later resolve it from explicit user direction or a separate memory input. A [bare writing prompt does not determine its intended contribution](../../theory/a-bare-writing-prompt-does-not-determine-its-intended-contribution.md).

If the simplification depends on choosing among materially different meanings, conceptual roles, evidence claims, or substantive conclusions, name that unresolved choice as a prerequisite. Do not resolve it as a compression edit. Semantic gates or the author must settle it first.

Return zero to three opportunities. For each one, give:

- the location and smallest useful quotation or section range;
- the important reader problem;
- the direction a revision could take;
- the compression findings it combines, if any; and
- the meanings, implications, or structural choices the author must resolve or preserve.

Do not present a rewrite as settled. A short candidate formulation may illustrate the opportunity, but label it as one possible resolution. Keep fact-checking, claim evaluation, and general completeness review outside this synthesis unless they are necessary to explain why the simplification cannot safely proceed.

## Running it alone

The [compression bundle](../run-compression-bundle-on-note.md) applies this synthesis after its four checks, under the bundle's own output contract. The inputs and output below apply when the synthesis runs alone.

### Inputs

The compression findings are explicit input files, one per check, such as the four check results under `kb/workflow-state/data/current/review/results/<note-path>/`. Run the synthesis alone:

```bash
commonplace-review NOTE --criteria compression-synthesis \
  --input core-claim-obscured=PATH --input branch-bloat=PATH \
  --input detail-overhang=PATH --input marginal-value-redundancy=PATH
```

Use only the supplied findings. Do not run a check, and do not look for other findings. The run keeps its result as a retained observation and writes no current result, because no freshness hash covers the supplied findings.

### Output

The caller names the output file. Write only that file; mutate nothing else. The output is a [review result](../../types/review-result.md) fragment with `outcome: report` and no `attack-outcome`. Each opportunity is one finding, zero to three in all. Give it `scope: passage` with its smallest useful quotation, or `scope: document` with no quotes for a section range or a cross-cutting change. Its `reason` states the reader problem and the direction.

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: passage
    quotes: ["<smallest useful quotation>"]
    reason: "<reader problem>; <direction a revision could take>"
outcome: report
---

# Simplification synthesis: <note title>

## Opportunities

### 1. <short opportunity name>

- Location: <heading and quotation or section range>
- Combines: <the compression findings, or "cross-cutting">
- Preserve or decide: <meanings, implications or structural choices the author must resolve or preserve>
```

Write `None` under `## Opportunities` when no opportunity clears the threshold.

# Review result

A review result records one assessment of captured target text against a criterion. Completion means the output passed deterministic checks, not that its judgment is correct. A report outcome is not a favorable verdict. Use this type for individual gate, compression-check, type-conformance and collection-conformance verdicts, and for critique, composition-friction, premise-decomposition and compression-synthesis reports and role reports. Do not use it for combined improvement packets or connection discovery.

## Content

Findings state what the assessed text establishes or fails to establish. Each passage finding quotes enough verbatim text to identify one contiguous span uniquely. A quote is matched after whitespace and typographic quote marks are normalized, so a line wrap in the target does not break it. A quote therefore identifies a passage and is not a byte-exact copy of it. A consumer that needs the exact span locates the quote in the captured target, which holds the exact bytes. A document-wide or absence finding explains the condition without inventing a quotation. Finding levels belong to verdict criteria; critique reports instead state whether the strongest attack lands and how the note engages it. An empty findings list is an honest completed result when no finding remains.

The body explains the assessment without repeating every structured finding. A critique preserves its central commitment, critique mode, strongest case, the note's response and constructive findings, including why an attack does not survive. Low-confidence no-surviving-attack findings leave the need for a domain check visible.

Each report method has its own shape, which the schema checks by the result's `criterion`:

| Method | Findings | Required body |
|---|---|---|
| Critique | constructive findings | `attack-outcome` in frontmatter; `## Strongest case against it`, `## How the note engages it`, `## Constructive findings` |
| Composition friction | the surfaced joints, thinnest first; each reason begins `UNSUPPORTED`, `THIN` or `HOLDS` | a `**Filter:** SURVIVES` or `DISSOLVES` line; `## Filter`, `## Thinnest joints`, `## For the human` |
| Premise decomposition | one per premise; each reason begins `HOLDS`, `DOUBTFUL` or `DEFEATED`, and a non-`HOLDS` reason names `LOCAL` or `GLOBAL` and `instance`, `prevalence` or `priced-exception` | a `**Register:**` line; `## Premises and counterexamples`, `## For the human` |
| Compression synthesis | zero to three opportunities | `## Opportunities` |
| Role report | one per dependent need, duplication or untaken recommendation; each reason begins `SUPPLIED`, `PARTLY SUPPLIED`, `NOT SUPPLIED`, `DUPLICATED` or `UNTAKEN` | `## Role`, `## Dependents`, `## Duplication`, `## Untaken recommendations`, `## Reach` |

Only critique supplies `attack-outcome`. Friction's filter line and the premise statuses route attention; they are not overall verdicts. A report criterion is named by its library instruction's identity, so moving one of these instructions requires a schema edit.

## Field ownership

The worker fragment supplies only `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, optional `attack-outcome`, and the body. Findings precede the outcome so the serialized verdict follows its rationale. The fragment is not a complete saved artifact. The controller completes and validates it; workers never assert hashes, execution identities or timestamps.

| Fields | Owner and meaning |
|---|---|
| `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, `attack-outcome` | Worker assessment; findings contain `scope`, `quotes`, `reason`, and `level` for verdicts |
| `description`, `format`, `contract` | Controller's result-format identity and expected verdict/report contract |
| `note`, `criterion` | Original target and criterion identities |
| `note-sha256`, `criterion-sha256` | Freshness hashes; the note hash may cover normalized watched parts, not exact bytes |
| `target-sha256`, `target-capture` | Exact assessed UTF-8 bytes and their retained repository-relative location |
| `observation`, `contract-sha256` | Execution observation and captured output-contract identity |
| `profile`, `model`, `run`, `launch`, `completed-at` | Requested execution configuration and observed execution provenance |
| `raw-output`, `raw-output-sha256` | Retained original worker fragment, distinct from this completed artifact |

## Template

Worker fragment for a verdict criterion; code supplies the remaining fields:

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: document
    quotes: []
    reason: "The claim omits the condition needed for its stated conclusion."
    level: warn
outcome: warn
---

# Review

## Summary

The conclusion needs its missing condition.
```

A critique fragment uses `outcome: report`, supplies `attack-outcome`, and omits finding levels. Its body retains the critique instruction's sections. Other report fragments use `outcome: report`, omit `attack-outcome` and finding levels, and follow their instruction's Output section. Neither fragment uses a terminal `## Result:` line. Operational production and publication belong to the review command, not to this type.
contracts.workflow-state/COLLECTION.md:
---
type: types/collection-contract.md
description: "Workflow-owned records used to continue a run, inspect a result, or recover an earlier decision; not the retained reports a clean checkout can cite."
---

# Workflow state

## Purpose

Use this collection to answer questions such as “Why did this run stop?” or “Which finding did the operator already decide?” A record belongs here when a named workflow owns it and reads it or keeps it to explain its work. Completion does not make the record disposable. Put an exact report readers need in a clean checkout in `kb/reports/retained/`; put an unfinished investigation in `kb/work/`.

## Layout and maintenance

The main repository owns this contract and the landing. New workflow payloads belong under `data/current/`, one directory per producing workflow. Older records beside `current/` are historical evidence, not inputs to current commands. Keep embedded paths in those records unchanged. The whole payload tree can be a separate checkout. A main-repository clone need not contain it.

Keep the identifiers, paths and evidence the owning workflow uses. Follow its filename, title and description conventions; do not rename a generated record for readability. Attribute inputs and judgments as required by the workflow. Staged candidates retain their destination format; keep exact captures unchanged. The state repository's README identifies what deletion loses for each workflow. Only the owning workflow sets the cleanup rule.

## Outbound links

A record may point inline to any KB collection to identify its inputs, outputs or governing procedure, or to an external source when the workflow records it as evidence. Keep references used by the workflow resolvable. Do not add formal footer links or topic tags to run records for discovery. Tags and links in an exact capture describe the captured artifact, not this collection.
